name: Headquarters and development
role_today: Headquarters, engineering, development of Spectrum and upgrades
role_proposed: Unchanged: one engineering centre for all sites

name: Andøya, second pad
role_today: In Norway's 2027 budget proposal (about NOK 646 M), state-owned, tenant not named
role_proposed: Readiness and redundancy: reserved slots for paid readiness and a fallback if pad A is blocked
capacity_basis: Half of a pad for Isar, the other half for other tenants (team setting)
trigger: A readiness contract with a European state, or more than 10 Isar launches a year at Andøya

name: Andøya, pad A (exclusive)
role_today: Isar's only orbital pad: flight 1 in March 2025, flight 2 reached orbit in September 2026
role_proposed: Core site for polar and sun-synchronous launches
capacity_basis: Pads × launches per pad (q3_pad_cadence); the site licence allows 30 a year for all tenants
funded_by: Lease for up to 20 years from 2021 (fee not public)
transport: Road and ferry from Bavaria (see research)
note: A failed launch can block a single pad for more than a year (Schingler)

name: Guiana Space Centre, ELM-Diamant
role_today: One of five laureates of the shared Diamant complex (term sheet 2022); no build date
role_proposed: Option for low inclinations and GTO, only with a European anchor mission
capacity_basis: Shared complex: a fifth of a pad for Isar (team setting)
trigger: An EU or ESA anchor mission and a build date

name: Spaceport Nova Scotia, Isar complex
role_today: Dedicated Spectrum complex signed July 2026: pad handover 1 Nov 2026, first launch 2028; 3.75 M USD per quarter, 30 months fee waiver after year one
role_proposed: Sovereign site for Canada and NATO and mid inclinations (45–98°); rockets shipped from Bavaria, integrated on site, no Canadian plant
capacity_basis: One own pad × launches per pad
trigger: At least 3 anchor launches a year (Canadian DND or NATO) by the end of the fee waiver, about 2030
note: Canada's DND leases its own pad at the same spaceport (CAD 20 M a year): the obvious anchor

name: Production plant in Canada
role_proposed: Not recommended: at 1–3 rockets a year a second line costs about twice as much per rocket
capacity_basis: Learning rate 0.7: a line building a quarter of the volume costs about 2× per rocket
trigger: Only if a Canadian local-content duty cannot be met by integration, launch operations and Canadian suppliers, and volume exceeds about 10 a year

name: Serial production plant
role_today: Builds Spectrum; vehicles for flights 3 to 7 in production
role_proposed: The single serial plant for every launch site; stages are shipped, final integration happens at the pad
capacity_basis: Today: Isar's plan of 4 launches in 2027. Proposed: design capacity of up to 40 vehicles a year from about 2030
trigger: A second plant only above about 30 contracted launches a year, or if a Canadian local-content duty cannot be met by integration, launch operations and suppliers

name: Engine and stage test site
role_today: Engine tests since 2020; second test site opened Feb 2026 for stage acceptance
role_proposed: Keep as the acceptance step for every stage; no Isar orbital launches here (Firefly is the anchor tenant)
